name: nanopb
notes: nanopb 0.4.9.2 runtime (pb_common.c, pb_encode.c, pb_decode.c) compiled from the pinned release tarball together with the generated bench.pb.c; code generated by the bundled nanopb_generator.py. The generator compiles bench.proto with the protoc bundled in grpcio-tools (libprotoc 35.1), not with $PROTOC 36.2: it offers no option to select a protoc binary. It consumes only the FileDescriptorSet, which is identical for this proto3 file.

Dynamic allocation mode: compiled with PB_ENABLE_MALLOC and every string/bytes/repeated field (including the repeated map-entry fields that represent map<K,V>) is declared type:FT_POINTER in bench.options, so decoding malloc()s/realloc()s like the other libraries and no array size is hard-coded. nanopb's embedded default (static fixed-size fields or callbacks) is not benchmarked.
Compiled with PB_FIELD_32BIT because the 16-bit default pb_size_t (max 65535) cannot hold the 64 KiB (65536 B) bytes blob of the large dataset.
wire_decode: pb_decode from pb_istream_from_buffer into a stack struct followed by pb_release inside the timed iteration.
wire_encode: pb_get_encoded_size (a sizing pass) + malloc + pb_encode into pb_ostream_from_buffer + free per iteration.
JSON operations are unsupported: nanopb has no JSON (ProtoJSON) support.
Maps are represented as repeated entry messages, so re-encoding preserves the fixture entry order and the output is byte-identical to the fixture.
